name: Brandon S.C. Chan
title: Pre-Doctoral Fellow in Economics
bio: I am a Pre-Doctoral Fellow in Economics at Yale University, working with Professor Costas Arkolakis. I graduated from Yale in May 2026 with a B.A. in Economics and Mathematics (with Distinction), where my senior thesis received the Wrexham/Heinz Prize and the Dickerman Memorial Prize.
My research focuses on spatial economics and macroeconomics, combining economic theory, computation, and history to study technological revolutions and long-run growth.

working_papers.abstract: Booms in infrastructure investment — railways in the 1840s, electricity in the 1920s, fibre in the 1990s — often coincide with investor exuberance and losses. But the infrastructure remains long after these episodes. I show that overoptimistic investors can correct a general class of market failure: agents with diagnostic expectations over-extrapolate good news and conduct irreversible investments, pushing what was once a market failure toward the efficient level. This mechanism — corrective overoptimism — is embedded in a model of spatial development with endogenous infrastructure and estimated on data from England and Wales, 1700–1881, spanning the canal and railway booms. Corrective overoptimism can be a potent channel of growth.
